Alpha-GPC.about: Acetylcholine precursor: for dementia - weak plus; in healthy people, 315-630 mg improves Stroop after an hour.
Alpha-GPC.caution: Alpha-GPC (L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine) is a precursor of acetylcholine. There are NO meta-analyses or systematic reviews in the database. There may be data in individual RCTs, but no systematic evaluation. Its popularity in sports nutrition is not supported by evidence.
effects: Memory (only in combination with donepezil in patients)
Alpha-GPC.food_sources: Purified phospholipid, not a product; Choline is found in eggs and liver, but not in the A-GPC form.
Alpha-GPC.guidelines: MA 2023 (PMID 36683513, 7 RCT): with donepezil cognition MD 1.72; solo vs placebo MD 3.50; There is no sports facility.
Alpha-GPC.how_to_choose: Standard 300-600 mg/day in courses; for dementia - adjunct with a doctor; A healthy person can’t wait for a “memory boost.”
mechs: Sports power and cognition in the elderly (weak)
Acetylcholine precursor in combination with donepezil
ADAS-Cog 12 weeks: −13.9% vs −0.9%; in combination with donepezil (119)
Acute cognitive boost in healthy people after a single dose
Stroop faster (d=0.61) after 60 min; N-Back/Flanker no difference (n=20)
Cognition with slight decrease due to T2D (1200 mg/d)
MMSE difference +1.7 is significant at 12 months; 6 months - no effect (n=36)
Alpha-GPC.myths: “Improves memory for everyone” - memory/fluency is not visible in MA. “Treats dementia itself” - effect with donepezil. “Boost for athletes” - only Stroop, n=20.
Alpha-GPC.name: Alpha-GPC
Alpha-GPC.onset: Healthy Stroop faster after 60 min (without N-Back); if it decreases, weeks of therapy.
Alpha-GPC.title: Alpha-GPC
Alpha-GPC.upper_limit: No formal UL listed - no toxicity data available.
Alpha-GPC.who_needs: Elderly with dementia - adjunct to therapy (by doctor); with T2D with a decrease - a weak signal; healthy - spot Stroop (n=20).
